audit.title: DataLink Provider Catalog

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a clean liftable statement — "DataLink offers a catalog of institutional and specialized market data providers." Each provider subsection also leads with the entity and partnership. Weak: there is no self-contained "What is DataLink" sentence, so a lifted chunk assumes prior context.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy — 1 H1, H2/H3, 0 level skips, 7 tidy sections (median 121 words). Weak: **0 tables** for what is fundamentally tabular content (provider × data type × asset class × coverage × feeds link); this is the single largest structural miss.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong — sourced figures throughout ("€230.8 billion", "2,900 buy-side customers", "75 countries", stablecoin scale "1 (very strong) to 5 (weak)"). Weak: vague quantifiers "robust," "many," "some" appear where a number would lift better.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 28 links, 27 external to provider sites and press releases — good for provenance of stats. Weak: **0 links to primary/canonical sources** in the DataLink docs sense; only 1 internal link, so the page is a leaf with no path back into the DataLink concept hub.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The SSA definition is crisp and verbatim-liftable. Weak: DataLink itself, and terms like "24×7 FX Feeds," lack a one-sentence canonical definition near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags, no head metadata captured. This is the weakest dimension — engines get no structured entity or freshness signal.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 code blocks. Largely a catalog page where code is not central, but there is zero integration path beyond "Contact us," so an agent cannot act. Feeds links exist for only one provider (S&P).

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "which providers / what data" intent well. Weak: no symptom- or task-phrased headings ("How do I access S&P stablecoin ratings onchain?", "Does Chainlink offer FTSE Russell index data?"), no lifecycle (integrate → consume) beyond a contact CTA.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Fluent, consistent product naming. Weak: "onchain" vs "on-chain" alternate within the page; one sentence ends without a period ("made available onchain").

audit.summary: This is a catalog page listing the institutional data providers available through Chainlink DataLink (Deutsche Börse, FTSE Russell, S&P Global, Tradeweb, NCFX), rich with concrete provider statistics. Its biggest GEO strength is specificity — 52 numerals with sourced figures like "2.08 billion traded contracts" and "€3.6 trillion" open interest. Its biggest opportunity is a missing summary table plus absent metadata: the page has 0 JSON-LD blocks, no canonical URL, and no dates, and it presents five providers as parallel prose sections that a comparison table would make far more extractable. The honest verdict: solid source facts trapped in an under-structured, metadata-blind page that engines will struggle to parse and cite as the canonical "which providers does DataLink offer" answer.

recommendations.title: Add a provider comparison table
recommendations.where: top of `## Data Providers`, before the per-provider H3s
recommendations.issue: five parallel providers presented as prose only; 0 tables
recommendations.change: insert a table with columns `Provider | Data types | Asset class / coverage | Availability | Feeds link`, one row per provider (Deutsche Börse, FTSE Russell, S&P Global, Tradeweb, NCFX).
recommendations.why: tables are prime extraction units; an engine can lift the whole answer to "which providers does DataLink support" from one chunk.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical, answer-first DataLink definition
recommendations.where: first line under the H1, before "DataLink offers a catalog…"
recommendations.issue: page assumes the reader already knows what DataLink is
recommendations.change: add one self-contained sentence, e.g. "DataLink is Chainlink's service for delivering institutional and specialized market-data feeds onchain from named third-party providers."
recommendations.why: defends against parametric priors and makes a lifted chunk stand alone.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata (JSON-LD, canonical, dates)
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `about` (DataLink, each provider), `dateModified`, and a self-referencing canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: freshness and entity signals raise trust/E-E-A-T and parseability; catalog pages change often, so a visible date matters.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased headings
recommendations.where: provider H3s and/or an intro FAQ
recommendations.issue: headings are entity names only ("FTSE Russell", "Tradeweb")
recommendations.change: add question-form subheadings or FAQ entries such as "What FTSE Russell index data is available onchain?" and "How do I access S&P stablecoin ratings via DataLink?"
recommendations.why: matches how devs/agents actually query; entity-only headings lose retrieval that question phrasing wins.

recommendations.title: Add feeds/data-access links for every provider
recommendations.where: each provider section (only S&P has "View available feeds")
recommendations.issue: four of five providers offer no path to the actual data
recommendations.change: add a "View available feeds" data.chain.link link (or "coming soon" with a dated note) per provider, plus a link to the DataLink integration/getting-started doc.
recommendations.why: gives agents an actionable next step and internal-link paths back into the docs hub.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with numbers
recommendations.where: NCFX section ("robust weighting"), Deutsche Börse ("more than 2,900" is fine; watch "some of the world's largest")
recommendations.issue: "robust," "many," "some" where a figure or named control would lift
recommendations.change: specify the control ("volume-weighted, outlier-filtered") or a count; drop qualitative-only adjectives.
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes; qualitative prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Normalize "onchain"/"on-chain" and fix punctuation
recommendations.where: whole page (both spellings appear); Deutsche Börse intro sentence missing terminal period
recommendations.change: pick one spelling site-wide; add the missing period.
recommendations.why: consistent terminology aids entity resolution; clean prose is independently rewarded.

antiPatterns: Repeated "TIP: Talk to an expert / Contact us" callout after every provider — mild marketing repetition that adds no extractable technical value.
One sentence lacks terminal punctuation ("made available onchain").
No tables for inherently tabular catalog content (structural, not stylistic).
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and last-updated signals are template/site-level; fix in the docs platform, not just this page. The CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata can be fully verified rather than inferred absent.
The page already references `llms.txt` — ensure this URL is listed there so the catalog is discoverable to agents.
Earned citations (third-party "which providers does Chainlink DataLink offer" coverage) are off-page; the comparison table above makes this page the easiest source to cite when they occur.
